new_indicators.name: Irregular payments alleged in connection with a grant
new_indicators.definition: Amounts that prosecutors, courts, parliamentary inquiries or authorities say applicants or promoters paid to officials, politicians, parties or their associates in connection with a programme grant or deal, outside the official price or fees (bribes, "gratuities", payments routed to politicians). new_indicators.notes: Proposed by fetch-cited-2-2026-10-10 for Comoros (AFP: "gratuity" of $105m to an ex-president, $29m to the promoter) and Austria (Der Standard: USD 2m and EUR 900,000 paid in connection with two special-interest naturalisations). Distinct from cbi_revenue_missing (money that should have reached the state) and investor_funds_misappropriated (money taken from investors).

ledger.contains: Al Khaleej, 10 Apr 2024: GDRFA Dubai director says golden residences issued in Dubai were 158 thousand in 2023, 79,617 in 2022 and 47,150 in 2021 (all categories). The rest is about AI in traveller services (out of scope). All three figures already in the data; nothing new.

CIU-website article, 10 Aug 2015: August 2015 CIP amendments (residence requirement 35 -> 5 days in five years, limited-time NDF cut US$250,000 -> US$200,000, lower processing fees without amounts, names no longer laid before Parliament); agent expects more applications. Event already in data; residence and NDF rules added.

Der Standard/APA, 27 Jul 2011: prosecutors charge Haider's ex-protocol chief, two naturalised Russian investors and a lawyer; payments of USD 2 million (Formula 1 sponsorship) and EUR 900,000 (after the January 2007 grant); EUR 150,000 left on a loan account (not a programme payment; not recorded). Event already in data; the two alleged payments added under a proposed indicator.

GDN, Mar 2022: NPRA spokesman: more than 1,000 requests and more than 400 golden residency permits since the February 2022 launch; eligibility (salary BD2,000 over 5 years, retiree BD4,000, property BD200,000), 90 days a year, 10-year validity, fee BD300 per person plus BD4. Both counts already in data; rules added.

Business Barbados, 20 Jan 2025 (article by a law-firm partner): SERP categories, investment and net-worth thresholds, real estate US$300,000, application, work-permit and renewal fees, validity, health insurance US$500,000, police certificates, dependants under 18. Investment/net-worth row already in data; other rules added. Lifestyle/tax paragraphs have no numbers in scope.

AFP via France 24, 10 Apr 2018 (Wayback capture): Comoros parliamentary inquiry report (Dec 2017): almost 48,000 passports, more than 6,000 sold outside legal channels, price EUR 25,000-200,000, state missed out on up to $971 million (~80% of GDP), initial deal 4,000 bidoon families for $200 million, alleged $105 million and $29 million payments. Two rows already in data; the rest added (the payments under a proposed indicator).

Reuters, 21 Aug 2018 (Wayback capture): Sambi formally charged and detained; programme began 2008; inquiry found at least $100 million of revenue missing; Dhoinine and 10 officials barred from travel; forgery charges. Charge event already in data; missing-revenue figure and travel-ban event added.

Al Jazeera, 13 Oct 2020: Cyprus to abolish the CIP from 1 November (abolition event already in data from the Audit Office report); AG opens criminal investigation; minimum "$2.5m"; Audit Office found at least 23 applications fast-tracked by the interior minister; ~1,400 documents in the Cyprus Papers (not a programme figure). Rule, count and AG event added.

OCCRP, 12 Oct 2023: gazette names vs budget naturalisation fees and CBI revenue (7,700 names 2007-2022; fees implying 19,000+; 1,664 names FY2017-18 vs ~4,000 implied; 382 names 2010-11 vs $15.6m revenue Jul 2009-Jul 2012; identical ~$6m in 2011 and 2012; PM: ~2,000 citizenships and ~$170m Jun 2018-Jul 2019 vs $80m in budget; ~4,000 gazetted Aug-Dec 2018; gazettes stopped naming citizens Mar 2019; 100+ names in leaks not gazetted; fee $750 -> $250 Oct 2017; base price $100,000; PM: NEP costs ~$5m a month). OCCRP's hypothetical "$38 million" (382 x $100,000) is a calculation, not recorded. All other figures now in data.

TI-España policy paper (Dec 2023, 31 pp.): Ley 14/2013 rules; MAEC FOI data on investor visas 2013 - 18 Sep 2023 (total, top 11 nationalities, real-estate shares, peak year 2021); Ministry of Inclusion FOI data on investor authorisations 1 Jan 2017 - 31 Mar 2022 (initial, renewed, administrative silence by nationality, Russian investment total); EU-wide and TI-2018 figures; UK Tier 1 and Portugal context; 2023 bill. Out of scope: 51,829/47,262/99,091 authorisations and their nationality top-5 lists, which cover all Ley 14/2013 categories (entrepreneurs, highly qualified, researchers...), not only investors; the 18,000 Chinese officials figure (not programme-specific).
